ops.title: trust: dead-peer verification race logs ErrNoVerifier ERROR flood; gate surfaces it as not-installed
ops.description:
Under machine load, a short-deadline wire client exits before the server finishes code-identity verification. SecCodeCopyGuestWithAttributes on the departed peer returns OSStatus 100003 (kPOSIXErrorESRCH — "no such process"), which trust/verify_darwin.go:231#ty6x wraps in ErrNoVerifier ("trust: no code-identity verifier for a configured requirement" — the fail-closed infrastructure classification per trust/policy.go:30#wnkx), and wire/server.go:468#z6tt then logs at ERROR under its infra-must-be-loud rule. codeidentity/verify_darwin.go:164#s7ry duplicates the same wrap.

Field evidence (local yBook-Pro, 2026-07-27): 59,553 "peer verification infrastructure failure" lines in capt-hookd.log (80 MB, no rotation); first occurrence 2026-07-24 07:43 (swarm era, then "run verifier child: worker: timed out"); flooding at multiple/sec under load 64–86 during the 11-lane release wave, all SecCode ESRCH. `capt-hook helper status` RPCs from a live client succeed concurrently — verification works for peers that stay alive; the flood is exclusively the dead-peer race.

The classification is wrong twice: (a) ESRCH on the guest lookup is a benign per-connection race (peer departed), not a missing verifier; (b) the loud-infra rule then makes it an unbounded ERROR flood. Client side compounds it: the ack timeout surfaces through captain-hook's gate as "signed host is not installed and ready; run capt-hook helper install" — a wrong remedy pointer against a healthy, serving host (captain-hook-side record filed separately).

ops.text: ESRCH (and equivalent departed-peer statuses) from the guest lookup is classified as a peer-departed connection event, never ErrNoVerifier; ErrNoVerifier is reserved for a genuinely unavailable verifier
A departed-peer verification race logs at most once per connection at debug/info level — no unbounded ERROR flood under load (both trust/ and codeidentity/ paths)
